akiec.name: Actinic Keratosis / Intraepithelial Carcinoma
akiec.description: Rough, scaly patches caused by long-term sun exposure. Considered pre-cancerous and can progress to squamous cell carcinoma if untreated.
precautions: Avoid direct sun exposure, especially between 10 AM and 4 PM.
Apply broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen daily.
Do not scratch or pick at the scaly patches.
Get the lesion examined by a dermatologist soon — it may need cryotherapy or topical treatment.

bcc.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
bcc.description: The most common form of skin cancer. It grows slowly and rarely spreads, but should be treated early to avoid local tissue damage.
precautions: Consult a dermatologist for evaluation and biopsy as soon as possible.
Protect the area from further sun damage.
Do not attempt to treat or remove it yourself.
Monitor for bleeding, oozing, or changes in size.

bkl.name: Benign Keratosis-like Lesion
bkl.description: A non-cancerous skin growth such as a seborrheic keratosis or solar lentigo. Usually harmless but can resemble more serious lesions.
precautions: Generally harmless — no urgent treatment needed.
Keep the area clean and moisturised.
See a dermatologist if it changes colour, shape, or starts bleeding.
Avoid rubbing or irritating the lesion.

df.name: Dermatofibroma
df.description: A common benign skin nodule, often on the legs. Firm to the touch and usually harmless.
precautions: Usually harmless and does not require treatment.
Avoid scratching or squeezing the nodule.
See a doctor if it becomes painful or grows rapidly.
Removal is optional and mainly cosmetic.

mel.name: Melanoma
mel.description: The most dangerous form of skin cancer, developing from pigment-producing melanocytes. It can spread rapidly to other organs if not caught early.
precautions: Seek immediate dermatologist consultation — a biopsy is strongly recommended.
Watch for the ABCDE signs: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variation, Diameter > 6mm, Evolving shape.
Do not delay — early detection dramatically improves outcomes.
Avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen while awaiting consultation.

nv.name: Melanocytic Nevus (Mole)
nv.description: A common benign mole. Most are harmless, but changes in a mole can occasionally signal melanoma.
precautions: Usually harmless — routine monitoring is enough.
Track any change in size, colour, or shape over time.
Use sunscreen to prevent new moles and darkening.
See a dermatologist if the mole itches, bleeds, or evolves.

vasc.name: Vascular Lesion
vasc.description: Includes cherry angiomas, haemangiomas, and other blood-vessel-related marks. Almost always benign.
precautions: Typically harmless and painless.
Avoid trauma to the area to prevent bleeding.
Consult a doctor if it grows quickly or bleeds often.
Cosmetic removal is possible via laser if desired.

unknown.name: Uncertain / Low Confidence
unknown.description: The model could not confidently classify this image. This is not a diagnosis.
precautions: Retake the photo with better lighting and focus.
Ensure the lesion fills most of the frame.
When in doubt, always consult a qualified dermatologist.
This tool is for educational screening only, not medical diagnosis.
